text:
sam-customer: Hi team — running into a 401 when I click "Connect GitHub" in the Console. UI shows "Authentication failed". Request ID: req_2026a9. Browser: Chrome 117 on macOS. Steps: Settings → Integrations → Connect GitHub.

maria-support: sorry about that — can you grab a HAR + console logs so we can see the failing request and headers? also confirm the exact time (UTC) you saw it. i can triage once i have that. :pray:

sam-customer: timestamp 2026-03-15 14:12:33 UTC. attaching short repro steps below.

eli-frontend: tagging in frontend. if it's a token/cookie issue we might see a missing Authorization header or a bad cookie. please capture both Network and Console.

maria-support: quick capture checklist (Chrome) — follow these and paste the HAR/console text or upload a zip: 1) Open DevTools (Cmd+Option+I) → Network tab. 2) Check ▢ Preserve log on navigation. 3) Check ▢ Disable cache. 4) Click the red circle to start recording (if not already). 5) Perform the repro (Connect GitHub). 6) Right-click the network list → Save all as HAR with content. 7) Console tab: right-click → Save as… or copy visible errors. 8) Important: find the failing request (status 401) and note the request headers, response headers, and request id header (x-request-id or similar).

maria-support: Quick capture (Firefox) — Menu → Web Developer → Network; check Persist Logs; reproduce; right-click → Save All As HAR. Console → Save Visible Messages.

sam-customer: got HAR and console. before I upload — need to remove tokens. what's safe to redact?

maria-support: please redact any Authorization header values, session cookies, and private email/user IDs. Keep request/response headers (names and status codes) and the x-request-id lines intact. For reproducibility we need: HTTP method, full path, status code, response body snippet (if small), and the time.

maria-support: small curl repro you can run locally (replace token and host as needed):
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider":"github"}' \
  'https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/oauth/start'
```
Run that and paste stderr if you get 401 — include the request-id header from the response if present.

eli-frontend: additional tip — when you open the failing request in Network, in the Headers pane copy the Request URL and Response headers; we specifically look for Authorization, Cookie, Origin, and Referer.

sam-customer: uploaded a zip (har + console.log + screenshot) to our internal support bucket — link: https://files.redwood.ai/support/har-uploads/1772000456-req_2026a9.zip (publicly redacted).

maria-support: got it. thanks. i'll attach to the ticket and escalate to eng with this note: 401 on oauth start, req_2026a9, user saw it at 2026-03-15 14:12:33 UTC, HAR + console attached.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-47 for elevated oauth failures — priority P2.

devex: if eng asks for local state, please export LocalStorage and cookies from DevTools Application tab: Application → Local Storage → right-click → Export, Cookies → Export. Add to the zip but mask tokens. This helps reproduce stale tokens or mismatched origins.

maria-support: if possible please also attach the result of running the curl above from the same network (home/office) — sometimes proxies rewrite headers. If you can't run curl, a screenshot of the full request in DevTools is fine.

support-upload-bot: Thanks — HAR received and scanned. No PII detected in visible fields. Link added to ticket INC-2026-47.

maria-support: next steps: eng will look at kernel logs for req_2026a9. i'll ping again with ETA. if you see this happening frequently, please add frequency + any pattern (same org, same user agent).

sam-customer: thanks all — lmk if you need anything else. :thumbsup:
